properties.title: NX-200 Nova AC 200 — Corporate AC Charger
properties.shortDescription: The NX-200 is a 22 kW single-socket AC charger built for corporate parking, hospitality, and retail sites that need faster charging and per-driver authentication than the entry-level NX-100.
properties.fullDescription:
The NX-200 steps up to a 22 kW three-phase connector, an integrated RFID reader for badge-based session start, and Ethernet plus Wi-Fi connectivity as standard. A 4G cellular module is available as an optional add-on for sites without reliable wired or Wi-Fi network access, such as remote hotel car parks.

It runs OCPP 1.6J and reports into Polaris Charge Cloud for device management, driver management, and billing. The NX-200 does not include dynamic load balancing or Plug & Charge — those capabilities are reserved for the dual-socket NX-400 and NX-450 — but its RFID authentication and optional cellular connectivity make it the right choice for sites that need controlled access without the cost of a dual-socket unit.
properties.targetMarket: Corporate parking garages, hotels, and hospitality venues that need authenticated, single-vehicle charging with the option of cellular backhaul at sites lacking reliable network wiring.
properties.keyFeatures: 22 kW three-phase output; integrated RFID card reader; Ethernet and Wi-Fi standard; optional 4G add-on module; OCPP 1.6J; Polaris Charge Cloud integration for driver and billing management.
properties.technicalSummary:
RFID authentication is standard, unlike the NX-100; the 4G module is a factory or field-installable add-on rather than a built-in feature, which keeps the base unit price down for sites with solid network coverage.

Like every unit in the Nova line, the NX-200 Nova AC 200 is covered under Northstar's Essential, Professional, and Gold service plans. Essential covers Monday-Friday business hours with an eight-hour remote response target and three-business-day on-site response; Professional extends coverage to Saturdays with a four-hour remote response and next-business-day on-site visits; Gold provides 24/7 coverage with a 30-minute critical remote response target and four-hour on-site response in supported metropolitan areas, with country-specific exceptions applying in Germany, Spain, and the Netherlands.

All Northstar hardware and software products carry a standard two-year manufacturer warranty from commissioning date, extendable to five years on hardware when bundled with a Professional or Gold service plan; warranty claims are handled through the same support channel as the applicable service plan rather than a separate process.

properties.title: NX-100 Nova AC 100 — Single-Socket AC Charger
properties.shortDescription: The NX-100 is Northstar Mobility Group's entry-level single-socket AC charging station, delivering up to 7.4 kW through one connector for sites where a handful of vehicles need dependable, low-cost overnight or workday charging.
properties.fullDescription:
Designed for small businesses, boutique retail locations, and employee parking areas, the NX-100 pairs a compact wall- or pedestal-mounted enclosure with Wi-Fi and Ethernet connectivity so it can be commissioned on an existing network in under an hour. It communicates over OCPP 1.6J, which keeps it compatible with most third-party charge point management systems as well as with Polaris Charge Cloud.

The NX-100 deliberately omits an RFID reader, a cellular modem, dynamic load balancing, and Plug & Charge — it is the simplest model in the Nova AC line, built for customers who want a low purchase price and minimal configuration rather than fleet-scale authentication or energy-management features.
properties.targetMarket: Small businesses, boutique retail locations, and organizations installing a small number of chargers for employee parking where per-session authentication and remote diagnostics are not primary requirements.
properties.keyFeatures: Single 7.4 kW connector; Wi-Fi and Ethernet connectivity; OCPP 1.6J compatibility; compact footprint suitable for wall or pedestal mounting; no cellular subscription required to operate.
properties.technicalSummary:
No RFID reader and no 4G module are fitted, so authentication and remote monitoring depend on the property's own network and, where used, an app-based session start through Polaris Charge Cloud.

properties.title: NX-450 Nova AC 450 — Premium Dual-Socket AC Charger with Plug & Charge
properties.shortDescription: The NX-450 is Northstar's premium dual-socket 2×22 kW AC charger, released in March 2026 as the successor to the NX-400, adding Plug & Charge authentication and a more accurate energy-metering subsystem.
properties.fullDescription:
Physically, the NX-450 shares its dual-socket 2×22 kW layout, integrated 4G modem, Ethernet connectivity, and RFID reader with the NX-400, and it targets the same large corporate and public parking segment. What sets it apart is Plug & Charge support: a driver with an enrolled vehicle can plug in and start a session with no card tap and no app interaction, using ISO 15118 vehicle-to-charger credential exchange layered on top of the same OCPP 2.0.1 stack the NX-400 uses.

The NX-450 also inherits and extends dynamic load balancing from the NX-400, and its metering subsystem was redesigned for tighter accuracy, which matters for sites that bill tenants or fleet customers per kWh consumed rather than per session. Firmware 1.1 (May 2026) addressed an early Plug & Charge certificate-renewal issue, and 1.2 (July 2026) improved metering accuracy further.
properties.targetMarket: The same large corporate and public parking segment as the NX-400, specifically customers willing to pay a premium for frictionless Plug & Charge authentication and more precise per-kWh billing.
properties.keyFeatures: Two independent 22 kW sockets; Plug & Charge (ISO 15118) in addition to RFID; integrated 4G and Ethernet; OCPP 2.0.1; dynamic load balancing; improved energy-metering accuracy versus the NX-400.
properties.technicalSummary:
Launched March 2026 on firmware 1.0; as the newest model in the Nova AC line it has the shortest release history of any current product, with two point releases so far focused on certificate handling and metering precision rather than new hardware capability.

Like every unit in the Nova line, the NX-450 Nova AC 450 is covered under Northstar's Essential, Professional, and Gold service plans. properties.title: DX-60 Nova DC 60 — Compact DC Fast Charger
properties.shortDescription: The DX-60 is Northstar's compact DC fast charger, delivering up to 60 kW through a single CCS2 gun for retail and hospitality sites that need meaningfully faster charging than AC without the electrical infrastructure a high-power DC hub requires.
properties.fullDescription:
The DX-60 is built around one CCS2 connector rated to 60 kW, with Ethernet and a standard 4G modem for connectivity and OCPP 2.0.1 for back-office integration. An RFID reader is standard. It does not support dynamic load balancing or Plug & Charge — those remain differentiators of the AC line's NX-400/450 and are not yet part of the DC portfolio.

Because it draws less current than the larger DX-120/240/360 units, the DX-60 can usually be installed on an existing three-phase supply without a dedicated transformer, which keeps installation cost and lead time down for retail and hotel operators adding their first fast charger.
properties.targetMarket: Retail parking and hotel forecourts that want a genuine DC fast-charging option for guests without the supply upgrade a higher-power unit like the DX-120 would need.
properties.keyFeatures: Single 60 kW CCS2 gun; Ethernet and standard 4G modem; RFID authentication; OCPP 2.0.1; installable on many existing three-phase supplies without a dedicated transformer.
properties.technicalSummary:
The DX-60 is the entry point into Northstar's DC line; its installation requirements are materially lighter than the DX-120 and above, since it does not require the ~175A-plus three-phase supply those units need.

properties.title: DX-120 Nova DC 120 — Corporate & Retail Hub DC Charger
properties.shortDescription: The DX-120 delivers up to 120 kW across one or two CCS2 guns, sized for corporate and retail hub sites that need to serve multiple vehicles per hour without moving up to a full logistics-hub installation.
properties.fullDescription:
The DX-120 splits its 120 kW output across up to two CCS2 guns, sharing power dynamically between whichever vehicles are connected. Ethernet and a standard 4G modem provide connectivity, RFID is standard, and the unit runs OCPP 2.0.1. Like the DX-60, it does not offer dynamic load balancing between separate units or Plug & Charge.

Unlike the DX-60, the DX-120 needs a dedicated electrical connection — approximately 175A three-phase at 400V — so site surveys for a DX-120 installation typically involve confirming available capacity at the site's main distribution board, and in many cases coordinating with the local grid operator if that capacity is not already available.
properties.targetMarket: Corporate campuses and retail hub operators who need meaningfully faster throughput than a DX-60 provides and have, or can secure, the three-phase 400V supply capacity the unit requires.
properties.keyFeatures: Up to 120 kW shared across one or two CCS2 guns; Ethernet and standard 4G; RFID authentication; OCPP 2.0.1; requires approximately 175A three-phase 400V supply.
properties.technicalSummary:
Installation prerequisites center on the ~175A three-phase supply; site surveys should confirm available capacity before committing to an installation date, since a shortfall typically means a grid-operator upgrade request with its own lead time.

properties.title: DX-240 Nova DC 240 — Modular Logistics Hub DC Charger
properties.shortDescription: The DX-240 is a modular 240 kW DC fast charger built from two 120 kW power modules, serving two to four CCS2 guns for logistics hubs and other high-throughput sites.
properties.fullDescription:
Built on the same core power module as the DX-120, the DX-240 pairs two 120 kW modules into a single system serving between two and four CCS2 guns, with power shared dynamically across whichever guns are in active sessions. Connectivity, protocol, and authentication are consistent with the rest of the DC line: Ethernet plus standard 4G, OCPP 2.0.1, and RFID.

Because it is built from the same modular power block as the DX-120, its installation prerequisites — dedicated transformer room, cable routing, clearances — closely resemble the DX-120's, just sized for a higher current draw: approximately 350A three-phase at 400V rather than 175A. Sites already planned around a DX-120 installation can generally reuse the same site-survey approach for a DX-240, adjusted for the higher supply requirement.
properties.targetMarket: Logistics hubs and distribution centers where multiple vehicles need to charge quickly and concurrently, and where the site can support a dedicated ~350A three-phase supply.
properties.keyFeatures: 240 kW total output from two 120 kW modules; two to four CCS2 guns; Ethernet and standard 4G; OCPP 2.0.1; RFID; installation profile similar to DX-120 but at higher current rating.
properties.technicalSummary:
The modular architecture means a DX-240 failure in one 120 kW module degrades capacity rather than taking the whole unit offline; the surviving module continues serving connected guns at reduced total throughput until the faulty module is serviced.

properties.title: DX-360 Nova DC 360 — High-Power Logistics & Highway DC Charger
properties.shortDescription: The DX-360 is Northstar's highest-power DC charger, built from three 120 kW modules for up to 360 kW total across two to six CCS2 guns, aimed at logistics hubs and highway locations with heavy vehicle turnover.
properties.fullDescription:
The DX-360 extends the DX-240's modular architecture with a third 120 kW power block, supporting between two and six CCS2 guns depending on site configuration. Connectivity and protocol support match the rest of the DC family — Ethernet, standard 4G, OCPP 2.0.1, RFID — but the electrical supply requirement is a step change from the DX-120/240: a DX-360 installation needs a dedicated medium-voltage to low-voltage substation supporting above roughly 400A, which typically means the site is planned as new-build infrastructure rather than a retrofit onto an existing distribution board.

This makes the DX-360 the right recommendation specifically for sites where vehicle throughput and dwell time economics justify the substation investment — long-haul logistics depots and highway rest areas being the two clearest cases in the current portfolio.
properties.targetMarket: Logistics hubs and highway locations with the highest vehicle-turnover requirements in the portfolio, and the budget for dedicated substation infrastructure.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud — Charging Infrastructure Management Platform
properties.shortDescription: Polaris Charge Cloud is Northstar's central charging infrastructure management platform, providing device management, driver management, billing, monitoring, remote diagnostics, reporting, and API access from a single SaaS console.
properties.fullDescription:
Every Nova AC and Nova DC charger in the current portfolio reports into Polaris Charge Cloud over OCPP, giving site operators a single place to see charger status, manage RFID cards and driver profiles, configure billing tariffs, and pull utilization reports across a fleet of chargers spanning multiple sites and countries. The platform is organized into modules that can be enabled per customer contract: Device Management and Driver Management form the baseline, with Billing, Monitoring, Remote Diagnostics, Reporting, and API Management available as the deployment scales up.

Polaris has been released on a calendar versioning scheme since 2024, adding the Remote Diagnostics module in the 2024.3 release, an API Management module with OAuth2 client-credentials support in 2025.1, and mid-session tariff-change support in the Billing module in 2025.4. It is also the platform through which dynamic load balancing on NX-400/450 units and charging priority rules from Orion Energy Manager are configured and monitored.
properties.targetMarket: Any Northstar customer operating more than a handful of chargers who needs centralized visibility, driver/RFID administration, and billing across sites, rather than managing each charger independently.
properties.keyFeatures: Device Management, Driver Management, Billing, Monitoring, Remote Diagnostics, Reporting, and API Management modules; OCPP-based integration with the full Nova AC/DC hardware line; OAuth2 client-credentials API access as of the 2025.1 release.
properties.technicalSummary:
Polaris is cloud-hosted and calendar-versioned rather than tied to hardware firmware releases; module availability is a commercial/contract decision, not a hardware capability, so a site can add Remote Diagnostics or API Management to an existing deployment without a charger firmware update.

Polaris Charge Cloud is supported under the same Essential, Professional, and Gold plan framework Northstar applies to its hardware line, adapted for a SaaS platform: incident severity determines whether the response target is a remote fix, a configuration rollback, or an escalation to engineering, rather than a physical technician dispatch, though Gold-tier customers still receive the same 30-minute critical response commitment for platform-impacting incidents.

All Northstar hardware and software products carry a standard two-year manufacturer warranty from commissioning date, extendable to five years on hardware when bundled with a Professional or Gold service plan; warranty claims are handled through the same support channel as the applicable service plan rather than a separate process.
properties.tags: software, SaaS, charging management, billing, API

properties.title: Atlas Fleet — Fleet Management & Charging Optimization
properties.shortDescription: Atlas Fleet combines fleet management with EV charging optimization, helping operators of company or delivery vehicle fleets schedule charging around routes, depot capacity, and driver availability.
properties.fullDescription:
Atlas Fleet sits alongside Polaris Charge Cloud in Northstar's software portfolio, focused specifically on fleet operators rather than general site management. It tracks vehicle routes and charge state, and since the 2.1 release has offered route-aware charge scheduling that times charging sessions around a vehicle's next planned route rather than simply topping up whenever a plug is free. Depot capacity forecasting, added in 2.2, projects how many vehicles a depot's chargers can service in a given shift window, which fleet managers use for both charger sizing decisions and daily dispatch planning.

A driver-facing mobile app, rebuilt as version 2 in the 2.3 release, lets individual drivers see their assigned vehicle's charge status and any route-related charging instructions without needing access to the full fleet console. Atlas integrates with Polaris for the underlying charger telemetry rather than duplicating device management functionality.
properties.targetMarket: Fleet operators — delivery companies, corporate vehicle pools, and similar — who need charging scheduled around route and shift planning rather than simple first-come-first-served charger access.
properties.keyFeatures: Route-aware charge scheduling; depot capacity forecasting; driver mobile app; integration with Polaris Charge Cloud for charger telemetry; optional Route Optimization add-on module.
properties.technicalSummary:
Atlas depends on Polaris for the underlying charger status and session data; it does not communicate with hardware directly, which keeps its own release cadence independent of charger firmware versions.

Atlas Fleet is supported under the same Essential, Professional, and Gold plan framework Northstar applies to its hardware line, adapted for a SaaS platform: incident severity determines whether the response target is a remote fix, a configuration rollback, or an escalation to engineering, rather than a physical technician dispatch, though Gold-tier customers still receive the same 30-minute critical response commitment for platform-impacting incidents.

properties.title: Orion Energy Manager — Dynamic Building & Charging Energy Management
properties.shortDescription: Orion Energy Manager provides dynamic energy management across a site's building load, solar generation, battery storage, and charging infrastructure, including charging priority rules that can favor fleet vehicles over visitor vehicles.
properties.fullDescription:
Orion sits above Polaris Charge Cloud in Northstar's software stack, taking a whole-site view of energy rather than focusing only on chargers. It manages building load balancing so that charging demand never pushes a site past its contracted grid capacity, and since the 3.1 release it has been solar-generation aware, shifting charging load toward periods of on-site solar production where possible. The 3.2 release added battery storage integration, letting a site use stored energy to smooth peak demand rather than drawing everything from the grid during high-tariff periods.

A core capability customers frequently ask about is charging priority rules: Orion can be configured to prioritize a company's own fleet vehicles over visitor vehicles when available power is constrained, ensuring operational vehicles reach the charge level they need for their next shift even during a busy period. This runs on top of the same dynamic load balancing that NX-400/450 units already support at the charger level, extending it to a whole-site, multi-energy-source view.
properties.targetMarket: Sites with meaningful energy-management needs beyond simple charger-to-charger load balancing — typically corporate campuses or logistics depots with solar installations, battery storage, or a mixed fleet-and-visitor charging population.
properties.keyFeatures: Building load balancing; solar-generation-aware charging; battery storage integration; charging priority rules (fleet-over-visitor prioritization); peak demand management; optional Solar Integration module.
properties.technicalSummary:
Orion's priority-rules engine is the mechanism referenced whenever a site needs to guarantee fleet vehicle charge levels ahead of visitor sessions; it operates at the site level, above individual charger firmware, coordinating with Polaris for charger-level control.

Orion Energy Manager is supported under the same Essential, Professional, and Gold plan framework Northstar applies to its hardware line, adapted for a SaaS platform: incident severity determines whether the response target is a remote fix, a configuration rollback, or an escalation to engineering, rather than a physical technician dispatch, though Gold-tier customers still receive the same 30-minute critical response commitment for platform-impacting incidents.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud — Billing Module
properties.shortDescription: The Billing module for Polaris Charge Cloud handles tariff configuration, session invoicing, and payment reconciliation for operators who charge drivers or tenants for energy consumed.
properties.fullDescription:
Billing is one of the modules available on top of the Polaris Charge Cloud baseline, alongside Device Management and Driver Management. It lets operators define tariffs by site, by driver group, or by time of day, and generates invoices or payment-provider charges automatically at session close. As of the 2025.4 Polaris release, the Billing module supports mid-session tariff changes, so a session that spans a peak/off-peak boundary is billed correctly across both rate periods instead of being charged entirely at whichever tariff was active when the session started.

Billing integrates with the meter-synchronization data every connected charger reports, and a mismatch between a charger's reported meter values and what Polaris expects is the most common root cause of a billing-session discrepancy support case.
properties.targetMarket: Operators who bill drivers, tenants, or fleet customers for charging — as opposed to sites offering charging as a free amenity, which typically run Polaris without the Billing module enabled.
properties.keyFeatures: Tariff configuration by site, driver group, or time of day; automatic invoicing and payment-provider integration; mid-session tariff-change support as of the 2025.4 release.
properties.technicalSummary:
Billing session accuracy depends on correct meter synchronization from the charger; review the meter-sync mismatch error code first whenever a billing amount looks wrong.

properties.title: Polaris Charge Cloud — Remote Diagnostics Module
properties.shortDescription: The Remote Diagnostics module, added to Polaris Charge Cloud in the 2024.3 release, gives support teams live visibility into a charger's connectivity, error-code history, and firmware state without an on-site visit.
properties.fullDescription:
Before Remote Diagnostics, first-line support on a reported charger fault relied on whatever the customer could describe over the phone or a scheduled site visit to inspect the unit directly. The module changes that by surfacing live connection status, recent error codes, and firmware version directly in the Polaris console, letting a support agent triage many faults — a dropped Ethernet link, a stale firmware version, a recurring error code pattern — before dispatching a technician.

It is particularly effective for connectivity-related error codes, since the module can often distinguish a genuine hardware fault from a transient network issue that clears on its own, which directly reduces unnecessary on-site visits under Essential and Professional service plans.
properties.targetMarket: Support and operations teams responsible for triaging charger faults across a distributed fleet of sites, where an on-site visit for every reported issue would be prohibitively slow and expensive.
properties.keyFeatures: Live connectivity status; recent error-code history per charger; firmware version visibility; faster fault triage before technician dispatch.
properties.technicalSummary:
Added in the Polaris 2024.3 release; most useful for distinguishing transient connectivity issues from genuine hardware faults ahead of an on-site visit.

properties.title: Atlas Fleet — Route Optimization Add-on
properties.shortDescription: The Route Optimization add-on extends Atlas Fleet's route-aware charge scheduling with active route re-planning, suggesting charging stops and timing adjustments based on live vehicle state and upcoming route legs.
properties.fullDescription:
Atlas Fleet's core route-aware scheduling, available since version 2.1, times charging sessions around a vehicle's next planned route. The Route Optimization add-on goes further: it actively evaluates whether a planned route is achievable given current charge level and, where it is not, suggests an alternative route or an interim charging stop before the fleet manager or driver needs to intervene manually.

The add-on draws on the same depot capacity forecasting Atlas introduced in version 2.2, so its suggested charging stops account for how busy a depot's chargers are likely to be at the suggested time, not just whether a charger physically exists there.
properties.targetMarket: Fleet operators running route-sensitive operations — delivery routes with fixed time windows, for example — where a vehicle arriving under-charged for its next leg is an operational problem, not just an inconvenience.
properties.keyFeatures: Active route re-planning based on live charge state; suggested charging stops accounting for depot capacity forecasts; builds on Atlas Fleet's core route-aware scheduling.
properties.technicalSummary:
Requires Atlas Fleet 2.2 or later, since it depends on the depot capacity forecasting introduced in that release to produce realistic charging-stop suggestions.

properties.title: Orion Energy Manager — Solar Integration Module
properties.shortDescription: The Solar Integration module extends Orion Energy Manager's core load balancing with solar-generation-aware charging, shifting charging demand toward periods of on-site solar production.
properties.fullDescription:
Introduced as part of the Orion 3.1 release, solar-generation awareness changes how the platform schedules charging sessions when it has visibility into a site's on-site solar generation forecast or live output. Rather than treating all grid-drawn energy as equivalent, Orion with the Solar Integration module actively favors charging windows that coincide with expected solar output, reducing net grid draw and, for sites on time-of-use tariffs, reducing cost.

It works alongside — not instead of — Orion's building load balancing and, since the 3.2 release, its battery storage integration; a site with solar, battery, and multiple chargers can combine all three to minimize peak grid demand while still meeting charging demand.
properties.targetMarket: Sites with on-site solar generation — typically corporate campuses or logistics depots — that want charging demand to track solar availability rather than running independently of it.
properties.keyFeatures: Solar-generation-aware charge scheduling; works alongside building load balancing and battery storage integration; reduces net grid draw and cost on time-of-use tariffs.
properties.technicalSummary:
Introduced in Orion 3.1; requires the site to expose a solar generation forecast or live output feed to Orion for the module to have anything to schedule against.

properties.title: NX-400 Gen1 — Original Dual-Socket AC Charger (Legacy)
properties.shortDescription: The NX-400 Gen1 was the original dual-socket 2×22 kW AC charger design, sold from 2021 until it was superseded by the current NX-400 platform in 2023.
properties.fullDescription:
Gen1 shared the dual-socket 2×22 kW layout and general market positioning of the current NX-400, but ran on OCPP 1.6J rather than 2.0.1, had no dynamic load-balancing capability, and used an earlier cellular module that was later found to have weaker coverage in areas with marginal 4G signal. When the current NX-400 launched in June 2023 with OCPP 2.0.1, dynamic load balancing, and an improved cellular module, it fully replaced Gen1 in the active catalog.

Gen1 units already installed continued to be supported under existing service contracts, but no new Gen1 units have been sold since the 2023 transition, and firmware development for the Gen1 platform has stopped.
properties.targetMarket: Historical only — large corporate and public parking sites that purchased the platform before June 2023. New deployments should specify the current NX-400 or NX-450.
properties.keyFeatures: Dual 22 kW sockets; OCPP 1.6J (not 2.0.1); no dynamic load balancing; earlier-generation cellular module; superseded by the current NX-400.
properties.technicalSummary:
No further firmware development is planned for the Gen1 platform; existing installations remain supported under their original service contracts but should be considered for migration to the current NX-400 or NX-450 at their next hardware refresh cycle.

properties.title: NX-400 Nova AC 400 — Dual-Socket Professional AC Charger
properties.shortDescription: The NX-400 is a dual-socket 2×22 kW professional AC charging station built for large corporate campuses and public parking facilities that need to serve two vehicles simultaneously from a single cabinet.
properties.fullDescription:
Each of the NX-400's two sockets delivers up to 22 kW, and the unit ships with an integrated 4G modem and Ethernet as standard, alongside an RFID reader for badge-based authentication. It communicates over OCPP 2.0.1 and supports dynamic load balancing, so a site with several NX-400 units — or NX-400 units sharing a circuit with other loads — can be configured through Polaris Charge Cloud to stay within a shared electrical budget without manual load calculations.

The NX-400 does not support Plug & Charge — drivers authenticate via RFID card or the Polaris driver app, not by simply plugging in. Plug & Charge, along with an improved energy-metering subsystem, is reserved for the NX-450, which launched in March 2026 as the premium successor in the same physical form factor.
properties.targetMarket: Large corporate campuses and public parking operators who need dual-socket throughput, dynamic load balancing across multiple units, and OCPP 2.0.1 compatibility with modern back-office systems.
properties.keyFeatures: Two independent 22 kW sockets; integrated 4G modem and Ethernet; RFID authentication; OCPP 2.0.1; dynamic load balancing across units on a shared circuit; no Plug & Charge support.
properties.technicalSummary:
Firmware has progressed through the 4.x line since 2023; version 4.8 improved OCPP session-resume handling but introduced an intermittent backend disconnect issue on dual-socket units under sustained high session volume, resolved in 4.8.1. Dynamic load balancing is a firmware-level feature, not a hardware option.
